page.layout: One page of running text, one column, with a running head at the top. Greek passages are set within the text. No marginal notes. A catchword-like abbreviation "Q 4" appears at the foot, right of the last line, treated as a signature.

main_text.p: Gens fuerunt adeo vilis, imperantibus Assyrius & Medis, ut regno eorum a Medis ad Persas transfato, velut vulgus αἰόνυμοι, victoribus prædæ facti, tandem Macedonib. servierint: donec progressu temporis tantas adquisivêrunt vires, ut non modo finitimis imperaret, sed & Romanorum magnis cladib.ab eis bello peti affecerint. Administratio gentis, post defectionem Macedonici Imperii, mansit sub Regibus, qui Arsaces ab Arsace primo Rege dicebantur omnes.

Pelasgorum lingua meminit Herodotus.] Quam Doricam fuisse auguratur. Ab Arcadib. autem ortos credidit Antiquitas: & Pelasgos dictos quasi πελάργας, quòd, antequam sedem sibi deligerent, ciconiarum more, hinc inde vagarentur. Eustath. Πλανῆται ἦσαν δὲ ἀποδεδεῖς πάντα χῆς γῆς. Πολύπλανον γὰρ ἔθνος καὶ ἑτοιμον εἰς ἀπαναστασιν. Mihi videntur dicti ab Hebræo phalag dividere, sejungere &c. (unde rivus dicitur) quasi rivulorum instar, in certas colonius distributi ac divisi.

Persarum lingua.] Quæ in tota fere Asia hodie locum habet: cujus in sacris libris non pauca exstant vestigia impressa, præsertim in Esteræ volumine: ut Achasch|weros, Parthemim, Esler, Hammedatha, Phur, vel Phurim, Gazza, Gimze, Susa, Zeres, Achasdar

page.notes: Greek words are transcribed as best as legible; accents and some letters in the Eustathius passage (Πλανῆται, ἀποδεδεῖς, πάντα χῆς γῆς, ἔθνος, ἀπαναστασιν) are uncertain and should be checked against the scan. Italic Persian names at the foot of the page are partly unclear ("Achaschweros", "Esler", "Gazza", "Gimze", "Zeres") and carry [?] in spirit; the final line is cut off by the page edge. The "Pelasgorum" heading line and the first word "Gens" begin mid-sentence; the running head reads COMMENTARIVS. Page is slightly skewed; some words near the binding are faint.
